source.label: Sirén names “the Dove at a Branch of Peach Blossoms” among the emperor’s bird pictures
Wikipedia lists Huizong as a representative of gongbi bird-and-flower painting

work.text: Best known among these are the Quail and a Daffodil in Marquis Asano’s collection … the Dove at a Branch of Peach Blossoms in Marquis Inouye’s collection
work.lead: Osvald Sirén, on the bird pictures he thought were very likely by the emperor’s own brush:

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

work.text: The bird and the flowering branch (or the plant) are placed at the one extremity of the design, the rest is empty ; but so perfect is the balance and the proportion between the painted volume and the blank space that a definite distance and atmosphere is suggested.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

moment.text: Kiso's white hawk and iridescent pigeon among peach blossoms show how he could create in the manner of Joki.
moment.lead: Ernest Fenollosa, using the Japanese names for Huizong (Kiso) and the tenth-century bird painter Xu Xi (Joki):

source.author: Ernest F. Fenollosa
source.title: Epochs of Chinese and Japanese Art, vol. II (new and revised edition)

matters.text: Dated 1107, it was painted when Huizong was about twenty-five and six years on the throne. It travelled to Japan, where Sirén knew it in a marquis’s collection, and it remains there.
